title: NYLF Medicine & Health Care
description: NYLF Medicine & Health Care is a pre-college program in which students role-play clinical scenarios and practice hands-on skills such as suturing, taking blood pressure, phlebotomy technique, and neurological exams under the guidance of medical professionals. The curriculum spans disaster triage, outdoor emergency medicine, medical ethics, and allied-health specialties including physical therapy, nursing, and biomedical engineering, and participants can earn 1-2 college credits through George Mason University. A typical day combines morning clinical-skills workshops, afternoon simulations and site visits, and evening activities such as speaker panels with medical professionals and social events. The 6-8 day program runs multiple sessions across summer 2027 on partner university campuses (for example Yale, UCLA, UC Berkeley, Rice, University of Michigan, and Emory), with both residential ($4,099-$4,799) and lower-cost commuter options, and is led by surgeons, resident physicians, nurses, and other medical and biomedical professionals.
selectivity_evidence: Official FAQ states: 'This is a selective pre-college program, but we encourage any student with a strong interest in health care and a passion for learning to attend. If you're curious and committed, you belong here.' No acceptance rate, essay, transcript, or portfolio is published or required, and the page offers direct 'Enroll Now' self-registration alongside a 'Nominate Now' referral tool - nomination is a marketing/referral mechanism, not a competitive gate.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: Interlochen Arts Camp
description: Interlochen Arts Camp's high school division (grades 9-12) is a residential summer program on Interlochen's 1,200-acre campus in northwest Michigan, offering intensive training in seven arts disciplines: music, theatre, dance, visual arts, film and new media, creative writing, and interdisciplinary arts. Students choose one-week 'Intensive' programs, three-week sessions, or six-week sessions; most programs of two or more weeks require an audition or portfolio for discipline-specific placement. Instruction is led by Interlochen's arts faculty in a conservatory-style structure of daily studio classes, rehearsals, and critiques, culminating in performances, exhibitions, or screenings depending on discipline. Tuition for the 2027 season ranges from $2,125 for the one-week Intensive to $10,500 for the six-week session, and need-based or merit-based financial aid is available for sessions of two weeks or longer (one-week Intensives are not aid-eligible).
application_requirements: audition or portfolio (for most programs 2+ weeks)
selectivity_evidence: Programs of two or more weeks that require an audition or portfolio review are used for discipline placement and are automatically considered for merit scholarships recognizing 'exceptional artistic talent and potential.' One-week Intensives and other non-audition programs are rolling/first-come-first-served rather than competitively reviewed.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: RISD Pre-College (On-Campus)
description: RISD Pre-College is a five-week residential program in Providence, RI for rising high school juniors and seniors, immersing students in day-long studio classes, critiques, and projects modeled on RISD's college-level curriculum, with a major area of study chosen for the program's duration and access to RISD faculty and studio facilities. In 2026 the residential program ran June 27-August 1 and cost $12,495 (commuter: $9,595); RISD's site states 2027 dates and pricing have not yet been posted, with 2027 applications opening in November 2026. Admission requires no portfolio or standardized test - applicants submit four short-answer essays instead - and RISD states that any applicant who demonstrates readiness and fit is admitted rather than having submissions reviewed competitively. The program serves roughly 560 students annually from nearly every U.S. state and dozens of countries.
selectivity_evidence: RISD's own admission page states: 'All applicants who demonstrate the ability and desire to contribute positively and benefit from the experience in their application materials are accepted.' No portfolio, transcript, or standardized test is required.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read

title: Parsons Summer Intensive Studies
organization: Parsons School of Design, The New School
description: Parsons Summer Intensive Studies (Pre-College) is a three-week, three-credit program at Parsons' Greenwich Village campus in New York City for rising juniors, seniors, and recent high school graduates ages 16-18. Students choose a studio discipline - such as fashion, painting and drawing, graphic design, interior design, or architecture - and attend class Monday-Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 3:50 p.m., combining project-based studio work, faculty critiques, field trips to art and design sites, and guest-speaker sessions with industry professionals. In 2026, tuition was $5,610 plus a $265 university fee (optional housing $2,180) across two three-week sessions (June 8-26 and July 6-24); 2027 dates and pricing had not yet been posted as of this research. Parsons' own program page states the program is open to all students regardless of skill level, and both residential and commuter options are available.
residency_restrictions: International students face an earlier application deadline than domestic students and must demonstrate English proficiency (TOEFL/IELTS/PTE/Duolingo/Cambridge English) if not previously instructed primarily in English; non-U.S. citizens/non-permanent residents need student visa documentation since this is a full-time, credit-bearing program.
selectivity_evidence: Parsons' own program page states the program is 'open to all students, regardless of skill level' who meet the age and application requirements - there is no portfolio review or competitive merit selection.

title: Tisch Summer High School
organization: New York University, Tisch School of the Arts
description: Tisch Summer High School is a four-week residential pre-college program in New York City for high school sophomores and juniors, built on Tisch's undergraduate curriculum. Students apply to one specific artistic track - Animation, the Clive Davis Institute of Recorded Music, Dance, Drama, Drama: Production & Design, Dramatic Writing, Filmmakers Workshop, Game Design, or Photography and Imaging (Animation and Filmmakers are juniors-only) - and take full-day training and classes Monday through Friday taught by Tisch undergraduate faculty, combining projects, professional-level technique training, and collaborative work that culminates in final presentations or showings. All students live together in NYU residence halls in Greenwich Village or Brooklyn with on-site residential staff, and the program awards four to six college credits along with a final grade. 2026 tuition was $12,012 for 6-credit tracks or $8,008 for 4-credit tracks, plus a $200 program fee and housing/meal costs; Tisch's site states 2027 tuition and fees are still to be announced.
residency_restrictions: Students must be at least 15 years old to live in NYU program housing, which is mandatory for all participants; non-U.S. citizens need a passport valid 6+ months past the program end date and may need an English proficiency exam.
application_requirements: two 250-word essay responses plus program-specific prompts
two letters of recommendation (at least one from a school representative)
selectivity_evidence: Tisch requires a minimum 3.0 unweighted GPA, a creative resume, full transcript, two letters of recommendation, and written essay responses as part of a competitive conservatory-style application process; no numeric acceptance rate is published.

title: Iowa Young Writers' Studio (Summer Residential Program)
description: The Iowa Young Writers' Studio Summer Residential Program is a two-week, in-person creative writing program in Iowa City for high school students in grades 10-12, run by the University of Iowa (home of the Iowa Writers' Workshop). Students take a mandatory core course - offered in fiction/poetry/creative nonfiction, TV writing, or playwriting - taught by graduates of the Iowa Writers' Workshop, alongside writing exercises, workshops, peer critique, and literary events and readings. Admission is based almost entirely on a submitted writing sample (up to 10 pages) plus a one-to-two-page statement of purpose and a recommendation letter from an English or writing teacher. In 2026, the program ran two two-week sessions (June 14-27 and July 12-25), cost $2,500 per session (covering room, board, instruction, and materials), and had a January 19-February 1, 2026 application window, with need-based aid including full and partial tuition grants available. 2027 dates, cost, and application window had not yet been posted as of this research.
application_requirements: letter of recommendation from an English/writing teacher
selectivity_evidence: The program states admissions decisions are 'based almost entirely on the writing sample,' evaluated by Iowa Writers' Workshop-affiliated readers; no numeric acceptance rate is published, but it is a competitive, sample-based review rather than open enrollment.
